speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you're here for knee pain after recent increased physical activity; to help me understand your condition, could you describe exactly where the pain is located and what it feels like?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age, the recent onset after pivoting in volleyball, and the worsening pain, could you point to the specific location of the pain on your knee and describe any swelling or instability you feel?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splains). The pain location over the medial tibia, combined with recent high-impact pivoting activity and a history of attempting weight loss (which may have altered biomechanics), is classic for this condition.
